hero_prop_criteria.center_of_focus: The story, a shot or a character's attention centres on the object.
hero_prop_criteria.high_frequency: The object is present in more than one scene/act.
hero_prop_criteria.transfer: The object passes between two characters.

scenes.heading: EXT. SABA ELIOR’S COURTYARD — LATE MORNING

hero_props.name: Yonah’s small lunch of five barley loaves and two fish
hero_props.description: Yonah’s packed lunch begins as five barley loaves and two fish; after he gives it to Andrew for Jesus, it is multiplied into bread and fish for the crowd, with leftovers gathered afterward.
hero_props.reason: This is the central miracle prop: the story, Miri’s lesson, and the crowd’s feeding all revolve around this lunch being offered, received, multiplied, distributed, and gathered.

hero_props.name: Miri’s cloth bundle of three honey-date cakes
aliases: one whole cake and half of another
hero_props.description: Three honey-date cakes wrapped in cloth; Miri guards them, later learns generosity through Yonah’s lunch, and finally shares them with Tav and Nim.
hero_props.reason: The cakes embody Miri’s conflict about scarcity and generosity, recur across the story, and are physically shared at the end.

hero_props.name: Miracle baskets and twelve leftover baskets
hero_props.description: The baskets used to hold, distribute, and gather the multiplied bread and fish; the final twelve full baskets demonstrate abundance beyond the original lunch.
hero_props.reason: The baskets are central to the visual miracle and leftover beat, pass between characters, and recur as proof that nothing is lost.

hero_props.name: Miri’s linen basket
hero_props.description: The basket Ima gives Miri to carry Saba’s linen; it also hides the cake bundle and later becomes Nim’s resting place.
hero_props.reason: It is handed to Miri, recurs as the carrier of key items, and remains part of the village-frame action.

hero_props.name: Folded linen for Saba Elior

hero_props.reason: The linen is the errand object that moves from Ima to Miri and then to Saba, recurring through references to his sleeves.

hero_props.name: Loaves-and-fish story scroll
hero_props.description: A small scroll tied with barley-colored cord and sealed with a loaf-and-two-fish mark; it opens the miraculous story world and later glows on the shelf.
hero_props.reason: The scroll is the portal and thematic vessel for the central feeding story, appearing before and after Miri’s transformation.

hero_props.name: Tav’s broken toy cart
hero_props.description: Tav’s small cart with a loose wheel; it marks his need when Miri first withholds generosity and becomes a shared repair activity after she gives him cake.
hero_props.reason: The cart recurs in Tav’s scenes and helps dramatize Miri’s change from passing him by to stopping, sharing, and helping.
